3: In the day of my affliction I earnestly sought the Lord; [even] with my hands by night before him, and I was not deceived; my soul refused to be comforted.
4: I remembered God, and rejoiced; I poured out my complaint, and my soul fainted. Pause.
5: All my enemies set a watch [against me]: I was troubled, and spoke not.
6: I considered the days of old, and remembered ancient years.
7: And I meditated; I communed with my heart by night, and diligently searched my spirit, [saying],
8: Will the Lord cast off for ever? and will he be well pleased no more?
9: Will he cut off his mercy for ever, even for ever and ever?
10: Will God forget to pity? or will he shut up his compassions in his wrath? Pause.
11: And I said, Now I have begun; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High.
12: I remembered the works of the Lord; for I will remember your wonders from the beginning.
13: And I will meditate on all your works, and will consider your doings.
14: O God, your way is in the sanctuary; who is a great God as our God?
15: You are the God that do wonders; you have made known your power among the nations.
16: You have with your arm redeemed your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Pause.
17: The waters saw you, O God, the waters saw you, and feared; and the depths were troubled.
18: [There was] an abundant sound of waters: the clouds uttered a voice; for your arrows went abroad.
19: The voice of your thunder was abroad, and around your lightnings appeared to the world; the earth trembled a quaked.
20: Your way is in the sea, and your paths in many waters, and your footsteps can’t be known.
21: You did guide your people as sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
